This band has been an absolute game changer for me. Coming to terms with needing to manage my activity has been quite the process, and I found it extremely difficult to really identify exactly what depletes me in the course of an otherwise mundane day as opposed to the obvious areas like going on long walks or being on my feet extensively. As someone with ADHD and some memory trouble, it was also increasingly difficult to track trends or similarities on my off days and during crashes as well.   With the band, I’ve not only been able to track things that I didn’t think about (getting dressed skyrocketing my heart rate was surprising), but I’ve also been able to find some vindication with activities I expected but couldn’t explain (simply sitting in the heat is my worst nightmare). This has also allowed me to bring real data to my doctors to support my need for medical help and monitor changes in my lifestyle that make things easier in the long run.   Ultimately, any issue I have with the band seems to be things that are not developed yet as this is a relatively new device, so I am greatly looking forward to what new resources arrive.   Two things that I personally would like to see are a wider array of scaling options for static tracking (a 0-3 scale for social/emotional/physical is pretty limited), and options to add symptom types in the evening check in (fatigue, headaches, and lightheadedness are the main ones but there are plenty of other symptoms that may be worth tracking on an individualized basis).

Super expensive but WORTH IT. It works very well and is so helpful. I have a few issues with it though: 1) you no longer are able to buy the arm band, you only can get the wrist band, and I hate the wrist band. I wish we were given an option there. 2) The actual band part is horrendous. Yes, the band is waterproof, but the fabric takes SO LONG to actually dry, plus it’s itchy. I wish we were given an option between fabric/silicone/rubber/etc. 3) The band is BARELY adjustable. If you’re thin, you can’t get the Velcro to stick. If you’re big, you can’t even get it on your wrist. It is NOT one-size-fits-all, and we should be able to choose different size bands.

I do love the app because I can see my heartrate in real time. I like that it lets me know when I am exerting myself. I don’t really understand the pace points. I do wish there was an app family could use to link up and also see my heart rate especially when I am home alone and incase I have an episode. I don’t like the new update where I pace points are above the heart rate.

I’ve since seen other users report the same thing. I ended up paying for a wrist band I can’t comfortably use and had to buy an arm band separately. I am genuinely excited to see whether this device can help me manage some ongoing health challenges, and the arm band is the only comfortable and realistic way for me to wear it consistently. I just wish that I could have the other piece and it was a lot cheaper, especially since I cannot afford to have it and it is definitely a life or death situation for me when I checked each of the things I have all minus 1. But unfortunately, I cannot afford the other piece in my insurance will not pay for it nor can I pay out-of-pocket and I am in a serious life or death situation. Otherwise I love so many things about this app. I just wish it was so much cheaper. Please make it more affordable.

I wish they were honest about their product and tell you the issues. Once I hear back and fix my visible or replace it I will update my review.

TLDR: I can't imagine my days without Visible anymore. I wasn't sure if it would be helpful with my autoimmune diseases (arthritis categories) but 4+ months in, it's a game-changer.   I have Ankylosing Spondylitis, Psoriatic Arthritis, Uveitis, and Psoriasis (phew!). I've been using Visible for about 4 months and it's helped massively for managing my energy daily and *trying* to avoid flares. Somehow the PacePoints are never wrong! It is also the best symptom tracker tool I have thus far, and gives me a tangible way to understand why I'm so fatigued (or sore) – especially when I don't realize how much energy an activity has taken. Having something that is proof that what I'm feeling ISN'T all in my head is validating and useful when it comes to recognizing symptoms.   I'm an active AS-er (move it or fuse it!) and Visible has also helped me balance exercise with rest.   Highly, highly encourage anyone with any autoimmune disease to try Visible.

In general, this app has been accessible and helpful. As someone who is visually impaired, I wish that they were full dark mode options and an ability to adjust size, because those two features not being in the app have made it very difficult for me to use over the past nine months or so since I’ve gotten the armband. Aside from that, I have loved being able to track my activity and gain a better understanding of my energy levels. I’ve had some issues with the band itself, but customer service has always been helpful and easy to talk to either through the app or their email support, though I will say that between an issue I had with the tracker itself not connecting to my device and then the band itself breaking recently, I’ve had months where I have not been able to use the tracker at all. It has been very frustrating because the subscription cost a lot of money and it’s for this reason that I don’t think I’ll be able to renew, simply between the cost of replacing the band and the cost of the subscription paired with the money I lost not being able to use it. I really wish the case was different because, again, I have really liked the insight into my health, but sadly I just can’t afford it.

I am garbage about listening to my body and Visible helps me pay more attention to myself. It's frustrating at times and sometimes I get mad that I need to rest because who has time for that? But you have to make the time to pace and learn to let things go before they get taken from you.   I'm still waiting for diagnosis but I suspect ME/CFS and POTS. I knew my heart beat fast and pounded sometimes but I didn't know how bad it actually was until I started wearing Visible.  Visible has helped me learn that my anger outbursts and mood swings aren't a personal failing of mine. They are another symptom of my exertion and exhaustion. When you're in fight or flight mode you don't have the energy to spare for emotional regulation. That's been incredibly validating and now it's something I can work on by learning what my worst triggers are, avoiding what I can, being more mindful when I start a task I know will be hard, and reminding me to take breaks and rest even when my frustrating body doesn't want to let me.  I bought the 2.0 band and was disappointed it didn't come with both straps. So I bought the arm strap separately. It's been hard to get the arm band to work. I'm plus size and squishy so it slips more than the wrist band and then I lose readings or I put it on too tight and the edges abrade my skin when I sleep. Having tattoos doesn't help! I have sleeves on both arms. I didn't see anything about visible not working well with tattoos before I bought it. It seems to read through some colors better than others. I have 2 pieces of bare skin where it fits but it's hard to keep it from shifting a bit when I move. I don't enjoy wearing anything on my wrist so not really being able to use the bicep band like I thought is a little disappointing. It would be nice if there was a third option where you could stick it wherever you want with a silicone dressing or something.  It would be nice if the charging cable was longer too. And if the app sent you an alert that it didn't detect a heartbeat for 5+ minutes. It's a little frustrating to lose chunks of data because it slipped and didn't record.  The heart rate monitor is pretty spot on with its accuracy. I was hooked up yo to telemetry recently and Visible was never more than a couple of points away from the hospital's heart monitor.   Overall though I like it, I'll recommend it, and I plan to keep using it daily.

I am really loving how well the Visible tracker helps me learn how best to pace myself throughout the day. I have CRPS and I run out of ‘spoons’ very quickly. There are some activities it tracks as higher on my pacing that I didn’t realize how much they took out of me. It makes so much sense why I’m still hitting crashes. I also love that it’s waterproof as I’ve been curious to see how something like showering/bathing ranks on the pacing scale. I’m really looking forward to some of the projected updates.  Especially if they are able to include sleep tracking data. I purchased Visible after seeing an ad from Chronically Jenni on Instagram. I did end up ordering the arm band after trying the wrist band for a few days. I wish there was an option to choose the arm band instead of automatically getting the wrist band when ordering. Or at least an option at ordering to pay to upgrade to an armband. Instead, I had to wait for my initial order to arrive, see that it was a wrist band, and then find the place in the app to order the armband. Especially since the ads that I’ve seen mostly show the arm band being worn.

I knew I couldn’t have that strap on my arm but I JUMPED at the chance for the wrist band! I’ve had it for 5 or 6days now and I love it! I love that it tells me how many pace points (estimated) I have as soon as I get up. And it keeps track of how many pace points I use and even suggests that I should take a break if I’m over exerting myself. It’s a great little tool to have! And it’s pretty cool that you can participate in medical trials. The only down side I’ve found is how expensive it is. I wish the price could be lower so more people could afford it. 💛😁

I wish there was a way to see where my pace points were without having to open the app every time if there was an Apple Watch integration that would be amazingI wish there was a way to see where my pace points were without having to open the app every time. Love this app wish it was also free if you bought the arm band I do hear that they’re trying to make it to where insurance will pay for the arm band and the app so hope that comes through but otherwise the free version is great. Love it for tracking all of my illnesses and my fatigue.

I was searching for a health tracker that could help me manage my energy because I have a tendency to go past my limits then crash. When I came across Visible I was intrigued because it’s designed for someone who’s dealing with a chronic illness, which is so different than other trackers. So, far it’s helping me understand how much energy I have, how much energy tasks take, and it’s helping me shift my mindset around what I “should” be able to do. I wish I’d had this throughout dealing with the illness I deal with.

I wish this would be more affordable and accessible to people like me who actually really need it to monitor the day to day stress tole

Right now I enter those into the notes section but it would be great to have a dedicated section and the ability to graph them out to show my doctors.
I love this app! It helps me know when I need to slow down and rest. Only thing I wish they would add is a sleep tracker and walking tracker.

I am not a data person nor am I very routine oriented, so this app has been a lifesaver for me. It is easy to use, easy to customize & allows me to track  what I need to without being pushy. The softness of the presentation makes me want to engage & makes me curious about my functioning rather than stressed about my lack thereof at times. I highly recommend this app for anyone trying to track their struggles AND wellness. It has all the bells & whistles for data junkies, but space for those who just need a way to track symptoms to share with our health providers.

You do have to be regular with the daily check ins and adding in your meds and supplements, symptoms etc. I’ve been using now for a full week and starting to see helpful trends and insights, and the check ins themselves are good reminders to be intentional about my time and energy. Would like to see more check ins available during the day like I previously wrote. But overall, and especially considering how affordable this app is, it’s a great tool.

I needed a symptom tracker and wanted one with additional features I could use to record and understand my condition. Bearable fit the bill and I do believe it is the best option for me! It is very adaptable and granular, which are among many traits I love. But I was slightly disappointed in a few ways others should consider before choosing this app... I think its adaptability works against it in some cases, as the interface is rarely optimal for the current task. If there was a focused view that opened with the relavent notification, that would make things like logging meds a little faster (it does for check-ins but nothing else afaik). The check ins are also a little confusing and convolute with other features. But it's perfectly manageable, and I understand that this type of development is rightfully often a low priority. Similarly, it is hard to make cumulative edits. If you accidentally enter data on the wrong date, which can be easy to do, there is no way to move/copy it other than manually. Finally, I understood the app to have more in terms of task management and journaling. It sort of has both, but you get more of a routine/goal reminder than a to do list, and 'journaling' is in the form of optional (usually Premium) notes. These are also a "cherry on top" features, but I interpreted the description as including these.  It's a great app and I'm grateful for the developers! I give 4 stars considering that a good and honest rating. I believe these points are being addressed already, and I intend to update my review as features evolve.

I saw that Apple Health added the ability to track an assortment of symptoms, and I have the occasional headache or stuffy nose … so I went looking for an app which might simplify my ability to record my symptoms to Apple Health.  I suppose what I visualized was my telling the app “Oh, I have a headache!” and the app asking me “How bad is it?” and my telling it “Mild,” and the app saying “Shall I ask you again in an hour how you’re feeling?” and my saying “Sure,” and the app waiting an hour and then asking “What’s up?” and my saying “Oh, I’ve been feeling fine for 15 minutes,” and the app replying “Okay then!” and recording into Apple Health “Headache - mild; from 1:10 to 1:55 p.m. on so-and-so date.” If I was lucky, I thought the app might also record to Apple Health that I’d taken two acetaminophen.  But mostly I just wanted it to write my symptoms to Apple Health, so that other apps could read them from there, or so that I might include symptoms — and their time and date — in an overall printout of Apple Health for my doctor, elementary stuff.  This app is not that!! This app is so-o-o-o-oo detailed, like it gets really granular in terms of the things it tracks and charts. If you’re inclined to record a lot of data into it, I suppose it could help you spot correlations between symptoms and the events surrounding those symptoms. It seems designed for people with truly debilitating chronic illnesses, who may need help narrowing down exactly what’s making their lives so unlivable.  And it may be great for people with debilitating chronic illness — I would not know, I’m a pretty healthy dude who intended to be a casual user. For me, for what little I needed, this app quickly overwhelmed me … and the subscription price, ye cats! For my intended casual level of use, this kind of pricing seems stratospheric. So it may be great for some people, but it’s not the app for me.  All of that being said, though, I’m quite surprised it DOES NOT sync symptoms to Apple Health. That’s quite an oversight. I wish apps which sync with Apple Health were required to specify in their App Store description what info it is exactly that they sync: this would save users lots of time. This app does READ a tremendous amount of info FROM Apple Health, but it does NOT write your symptoms TO Apple Health.  So I give it three stars in terms of its utility to me: it looks like it works, it’s extraordinarily detailed, it’s just not what I need right now, and it does NOT do the one thing I’d hoped it would do. But for you, if you have a life-upending chronic illness, it may be a five-star app or even a six-star app. Luckily for me I’m in good shape, and to be honest, I hope I continue NOT needing this app.  If the day comes that I do, though, I would still be disappointed if they hadn’t added the ability to WRITE symptoms TO Apple Health for possible integration with other apps; this seems like the whole point of having a centralized repository of health information!

If you’re like me and you’re dealing with health problems, you’re probably doing so many things all at once just to see if something helps and find some relief. Medications, exercise, therapy, fill in the blank. And then you experience a setback and you think “Are any of the things I’m doing even helping? Am I making any progress?” This app takes care of that for you. The premium version is so customizable. You can input any habit, activity, symptom, medication, etc. that you want. And the automatic correlations that the app finds between your habits and outcomes is so helpful. I’ve only been using the app for two weeks, and I can already see that when I go for walks, my weird leg pain improves. So that motivates me to go for more walks. I probably wouldn’t have figured that out on my own because there are just so many variables that go into my day. It’s just little things like that, and having that knowledge, that makes a huge difference in your health journey. I’m withholding one star because wish I could track my cycle. I manually created factors for each phase of the cycle, but I wish it was a built in feature. Our hormones really have a huge impact on every aspect of our life, and it would help me and a lot of women to have that data. And it’s something we could easily show our GYN too for them to be able to say “yeah, that’s normal,” or “you get extremely depressed when you’re menstruating, that’s not healthy and we need to look into that.” But other than that I love the app and know that it’s going to be very beneficial the more I use it.

I never write reviews when they ask for it. I’m sick. I don’t have the time or energy to write reviews. If you’re here reading this review, I’m sure you’re in the same boat. You’re sick too. You are weak and tired too. You don’t have time or energy. But this app is incredible. It doesn’t take time. It saves time. It makes time. It makes joy. It makes ease. It makes me smile. It has a bear on it. Trust me. It’s well executed and brilliantly thought out, even the free version which is what I’m using. I’ve used it for a week and even with my cognitive impairments it’s incredibly intuitive and easy to use. I LOVE it. Genuinely. It’s so easy to use, to customize and personalize, to track, to make your own for any and all your health needs. I’ve shown it to everyone. In one week it’s made all 3 of my doctors appointments go so much smoother. It’s made taking and tracking all 15 daily medications go by so much easier. Tracking my food too to make sure I eat despite forgetting and the nausea and the appetite being gone. It has the ability to remind you to do things. Take medicine for example. Tracking my many symptoms too. Even the little gratitude tracker is a nice bonus. And the mood tracker is a nice bonus to have me consciously think about how I’m feeling emotionally not just physically. All of it is brilliant. I love that I can add in my own symptoms and my own emotions, for when I feel ennui or emotionally energized or on fire or proud, or symptoms like ‘senility’ or other things that don’t come pre-set. It’s all just so incredible and I could go on and on. I wish I could pay for it to use all its goodness but the free version is nice too. Just to track what I do. Do yourself a favor and just download this, if there’s anything at all up with your health. Yeah, just do it. Make yourself beary happy.

The new update has made it so you can swipe to dismiss/skip reminders which is nice but it puts the oldest ones on the bottom. Oldest used to be on top and I could see them in order. Now it’s backwards and I’m missing stuff because I’m used to going top to bottom not bottom to top. Change it back please.  UPDATE TO DEV. RESPONSE:  Well, it’s easy to miss reminders you are passed due on when they are on the bottom and literally hidden in a drop down with upcoming ones on top… Since you have coded the app both ways, maybe you should have a sort option so the user can choose what works for them instead of assuming? And clicking into reminders does no good, it’s confusing at a glance having them opposite. Mid-as-well have the option to hide reminders on the daily screen then. I’ve gone back to Apple Health until this is fixed… Missed reminders on the bottom  and hidden by upcoming ones is just hilariously ridiculous.

Found this app through a woman on Instagram, and it’s superb. Insanely thorough and detailed basic free version. Only thing I wish it was capable of, was adding a picture of my blood pressure cuff for home measurements. And that’s fine though, I can take a picture and find the photo in my gallery to coordinate with the logged BP. Literally 0 complaints. Thank you for an amazing app while I am in a confusing time with my health.
So far this app is great. I do wish they had a widget to go on the home screen. But otherwise cannot complain.

I started out using the Bearable app, hoping I could get some good insights about my health and mental health and what factors have impacts on various aspects of my health. Bearable’s data insights were, to put it mildly, useless. They didn’t actually make sense and you couldn’t even compare half of the information you’d been collecting for ages in hopes of getting good, interesting insights. But then I found Guava. I will admit that Bearable’s UI & UX is a bit more visually appealing and intuitive, but Guava reigns supreme in literally every other way.   You can connect your medical records and Apple Health data, as well as a bunch of other apps and whatnot. You can track nearly everything, and the integration with my healthcare providers’ system is priceless, especially for me as a cancer patient who is seeing doctors and getting bloodwork/vitals done super often. I freaking LOVE this app! I am so stoked about learning all these interesting things about my health and my environment and habits. It’s just so cool.  The only thing I wish it had was integration with the myAir app, so I could track the data from my CPAP machine and get insights about those things. But maybe someday—the devs are pretty great about updating the app and adding new features, so hey, maybe I’ll get lucky! In any case, this is an amazing app and has totally changed my outlook on my health—by sort of gamifying health tracking in a way, it’s encouraged me to be more mindful of my health and the things that impact it, and to do things that are good for me.

It can connect and access a terrifying amount of data - at a time when that definitely is risky and feels costly against the need to insure privacy etc. so buyer beware. But of all the dozens (at least) of ways I have tried to track all of the correlations to the intense pain and symptoms of my autoimmune disease and food and weather- nothing comes close to being as easy and efficient by a mile. I have been consistently tracking for over a month and finally upgraded to track insights. It wasn’t necessary - but it did point out aspects of weather and heart rate correlations I had never considered - and that is valuable if only to point out to me what I have not given attention to. So I give it 4 stars - but this is in part unfair perhaps - because the star subtracted is mostly left off for reasons that are not the fault of the app entirely - like the data exploitation and vulnerability of anyone in the US. If you are someplace with socialized medicine you may feel more comfortable, or someone who’s government doesn’t feel bent towards fascism that is deeply tied to data farming and exploitation than you are probably less anxious than me about the caveats. The app clearly needs the data to perform - so perhaps a clear, straightforward explanation of how it is being anonymized in detail - and how it’s is not lumped and dumped on a server but rather distributed into different encrypted sets or some other reassurance would do a lot to reassure me.  One request for developers - and this is made with the clear appeal to also not change anything else because it is absolutely perfect otherwise (seriously! It’s brilliant!)  If symptom groups could be used in insights that would be hugely helpful. It is bothersome to try and look for correlations one symptom at a time when you have a lot of- but the groups related to specific conditions might even shed more light on actual correlations. I have thought about adding a super category as a symptom and going back to crunch a sort of median - but it actually seems like a fair simple programming addition that would make a huge different to many users. Thanks in advance!   And regarding the cost. It is fair- with the amount I sink into supplements and co-pays the value of this app stands out as actually providing a huge amount of benefit for the cost. If I ran a clinic, I would provide it to patients. My ability to self report medication adherence is fairly bad - but the app, if used, can give an exact record - in addition to trillions of other benefits. There is a lot of power in the data - and in this way I think it should stay entirely in the hands of the patients, but this will benefit everyone by empowering them to communicate more in detail and provide informed observations (in a quantified format that Dr.’s can refer to over time) to their practitioners.

I’m a chronic illness girly and let me tell you, i’m always getting tests done and seeing random doctors for things that I can’t even pronounce correctly half the time and this app has made it so much easier to follow along with my results and know what I should be paying attention to. I love that I could sync my Apple Watch data to it too! I wish it had a few minor improvements but other than that, great app!!

I’ve been trying out different health trackers for a while, and they all have 1-2 things they excel at while everything else falls behind. I think Guava is finally what I’ve been looking for.  It connects to devices, Apple Health, and most of my patient portals. It tracks appointments, medications, symptoms (with body “heat maps”!) measurements, and more. It lets you add custom categories, entries, events, and more which is great for my weirder symptoms and specific triggers. It’s great for data nerds like me!  My favorite part is that everything you need is available with the free version! The premium subscription has some great features, but it’s mostly advanced insights and easier transfers from doctor’s notes. All the tracking and analysis features I need I can get for free.   My one request is that I wish it had more advanced analysis to do with length of symptoms. I have chronic headaches, and while there is a way to put a start and end time in my log, there’s not any good way to see what affects the length of my headaches (or the average length or anything like it). Regardless, Guava is a great app and I’m so glad I found it.
Great app for tracking all my health issues. But a widget would be helpful to remind me to fill it out every night.

TLDR: this is the perfect symptom tracker/health management app. Stop your search and download it.   The free version is a fully functional app by itself that doesn’t try to give you half-features to force you into getting premium (premium just offers new cool features).    I’ve spent countless hours trying to find an app that will help me track symptoms of chronic illness for myself and my doctors. I thought the features I was looking for were fairly common sense, but I couldn’t find a tracker that checked all my boxes. I read articles ranking apps and downloaded multiple options but none were quite right. Some didn’t even have a free version that allowed someone to evaluate enough of its features and export the data to make it worth the time and effort of using it for a trial period. I was close to giving up, searching random key words in the App Store, when I stumbled upon Guava.    At first I thought Guava was too good to be true. I downloaded it and saw almost immediately that it has everything I was looking for plus so much more that I didn’t even know I wanted until now. I do wish there was an option for a one-time purchase, even if it was a bit pricey, but I understand that can be difficult for developers. And at least the subscription prices are very reasonable.  I paid for premium within a day of trying out the free version, and I usually take ages to make these decisions.   I rarely write reviews but this is a gem. I’ll try to update once I’m able to test it long-term, but it’s already easy to tell that this is going to make my difficult health journey that much easier to manage.

This app is everything I could have hoped for and constantly being improved even!! The AI feature and insights are so helpful, symptom tracker is easiest ever, integrates well with medial records! It’s my favorite app!! Amazing for chronic health conditions but I think anyone would like it, even just for food tracking and activity!

The app is very well designed with intuitive UI especially for iPad. It would be great if you can consider supporting devices from Abbott labs (Contour Next One glucose meters). Also though the webpage says Healow health system is supported, am not able to find a way to connect to Healow.
I have searched for something like this to track fibromyalgia. I do wish it pulled in local weather, environment and allergen levels.
This app majorly helps me keep track of everything going on for my health!  Only thing I think would be beneficial would be if the profile had a section to list all my providers with their info
